newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen testing correction lows.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen testing correction lows.

text.p: A short-term bounce in Wall Street stocks is at its end, setting the stage for equities to re-test the lows set last week, analysts said.
Technicians said they saw little evidence the market's corrective phase is over despite recent gains. Several say stocks need to undergo another decline before resuming their secular climb.
"My sense is we're about three-quarters of the way through this down wave," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co.
"My suspicion is we'll re-test the lows before we get up to about the 6750 area (on the Dow)," he said.
The Dow was off about 15 points at 6548 Thursday afternoon. The S&P 500 index was off about two at 759.
Analysts said the next phase of the correction is also important because it offers an opportunity infrequently seen in the past two years to locate a significant support level.
"It's been difficult, because there haven't been many stopping points, to know where support is," said Elaine Yager, manager of technical analysis at Herzog, Heine, Geduld.
Yager said a re-test of last week's intraday lows -- which she put at 6404.84 on the Dow and about 744 on the S&P 500 -- would offer an important technical read for other reasons.
"On the S&P, 746 represented a one-third pullback of the leg up from July 1996," she said. "So if this market is going to resume on the downside, that's the level that has to be broken."
Technicians said there were positive signs emerging. Bearish sentiment is on the rise, reflected in the fact that bears have outnumbered bulls in several investor surveys.
However, they stressed there were still too many indicators pointing to a downward move. Several analysts pointed to volume levels as a key indicator.

"Odds for a downtrend in price are significantly higher when volume is in a downtrend," said Alan Newman, technical analyst at H.D. Brous & Co Inc. "There is no question that bull markets thrive on volume."
Likewise, some analysts said they would be reluctant to call an end to the correction phase until stocks endured a decline on very heavy volume.
"That's been a problem, that the volume hasn't been there," Green said. "You want to see climactic selling. We'll probably need a more than 683 million share day."
